title: ACR Context Fabric Common Shapes v1

evidence_window.description: CHAOS-3900 W1: legal ONLY when axis is current -- every other axis's own as_of/start/end already IS the window that axis answers for.

RequestedEvidenceWindow.description: CHAOS-3900 W1: the caller's own evidence-window intent. Structurally cannot carry provenance/class/confidence -- those are server-computed. RelativeID all_time requires start/end to both be absent; every other shape requires both.

not.description: CHAOS-3900 W1 (codex round 7): the anyOf above proves AT LEAST ONE of relative_id/start+end is present, but does not by itself forbid a partial bound alongside a relative_id (e.g. relative_id+start with no end) -- that shape satisfies the anyOf's first branch regardless of how incomplete the bounds are. This guard closes exactly that gap: whichever of start/end is present, the other must be too, matching validate_context_fabric_window.go's validate() line 49 ("requires an ordered start and end") for every non-all_time shape, independent of whether relative_id is also present.

EffectiveEvidenceWindow.description: CHAOS-3900 W1: the window an answer actually speaks for once canonicalization has run. Server-computed; never accepted from the wire.

not.description: CHAOS-3900 W1 (codex round 7): mirrors RequestedEvidenceWindow's own completeness guard -- the anyOf above proves at least one of relative_id/start+end is present but does not forbid a partial bound alongside a relative_id. See RequestedEvidenceWindow's identical clause for the full explanation.

RelativeWindowID.description: CHAOS-3900 W1: the closed, server-owned relative-window identifier registry (design brief v5.2 §5.1).

WindowOption.description: CHAOS-3900 W1: one server-offered window choice, minted onto a stored result so a later turn can confirm it via winr_ receipt redemption. Start/end are the FROZEN absolute bounds computed at offer time.

allOf.description: CHAOS-3900 W1: a non-all_time relative_id's bounds are the FROZEN offer-time computation, so both must be present -- mirrors window.validate() lines 33-52's non-all_time branch (via WindowOption.Validate's own additional relative_id-non-all_time-requires-bounds check, validate_context_fabric_window.go:115-117).

CHAOS-3900 W1 (codex round 7): all_time forbids any bound -- mirrors window.validate() lines 37-40, which the original if/then above never encoded because its own 'if' matches only the non-all_time direction. Deliberately does NOT also fire when relative_id is absent: an option with no relative_id and BOTH bounds present is a legal explicit-bounds-only shape (window.validate() lines 43-52), which this clause must not forbid.

anyOf.description: CHAOS-3900 W1 (codex round 7): baseline presence -- an option with neither relative_id nor any bound satisfies neither if/then above (both require relative_id to fire) and so previously passed schema validation despite window.validate() lines 43-47 rejecting it ('requires a relative_id or explicit bounds').

not.description: CHAOS-3900 W1 (codex round 7): completeness guard, identical to RequestedEvidenceWindow's own -- the anyOf above is satisfied by a relative_id present alongside only ONE bound (it does not check the bound pair for completeness), which window.validate() line 49 rejects regardless of relative_id. Forbids exactly-one-of-start/end unconditionally.

WindowExpandOption.description: CHAOS-4314; semantics widened CHAOS-4336: a gated window's recommendation that a wider tier is available to try -- presence is a statement about tier ordering alone, never evidence that an offers-only pool was found non-empty (see candidate_label/candidate_kind, now genuinely optional). receipt_id/option_id/label/relative_id are copied VERBATIM from one entry the same result's own window_options already carries (no fresh bounds here -- redemption applies the referenced WindowOption's own frozen start/end, never a value on this type).

WindowClarification.description: CHAOS-3900 W1: every window option a stored result offered. RESIDUAL, SERVER-SIDE-ONLY INVARIANT (codex round 7): options.uniqueItems below rejects two options that are structurally identical in EVERY field, but standard JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) has no keyword to express uniqueness on a DERIVED SUBSET of fields -- so two options differing only in, say, label but sharing the same receipt_id or option_id pass this schema even though ContextFabricWindowClarification.Validate (validate_context_fabric_window.go, the design brief's own 'm5' invariant) rejects them. That per-field uniqueness is enforced by Go alone; it is not expressible here.

TemporalLabel.description: The time an answer actually speaks for on a historical time axis (CHAOS-3781, AC-3781-2). Absent on the current axis. Effective is always narrower than or equal to requested; an answer may speak for less time than was asked about, never more.

SubjectKind.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: the closed ContextFabricSubjectKind vocabulary, given its own $def so KindOption/AnchorOption/HandleOption/AcceptedGrammar can $ref it directly rather than each re-duplicating the enum inline the way SubjectRef/SubjectCandidate/etc. still do at their own call sites.

WindowBoundReceipt.description: CHAOS-3900 W1: same shape as BoundSubjectReceipt, but receipt_id is additionally constrained to the closed winr_ namespace (design brief section 5, pivot brief section 2's closed kindr_/ancr_/handr_/winr_ set) -- a separate type, not a reuse of BoundSubjectReceipt, so the schema itself rejects a subject-namespaced id in prior_window_receipts the same way validate_context_fabric_request.go does.

KindBoundReceipt.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: same shape as BoundSubjectReceipt, but receipt_id is additionally constrained to the closed kindr_ namespace (pivot-intent design brief section 2's closed kindr_/ancr_/handr_/winr_ set) -- mirrors WindowBoundReceipt's own reasoning exactly.

AnchorBoundReceipt.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: same shape as BoundSubjectReceipt, but receipt_id is additionally constrained to the closed ancr_ namespace -- mirrors WindowBoundReceipt's own reasoning exactly.

HandleBoundReceipt.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: same shape as BoundSubjectReceipt, but receipt_id is additionally constrained to the closed handr_ namespace -- mirrors WindowBoundReceipt's own reasoning exactly.

CandidateBoundReceipt.description: CHAOS-4012: same shape as BoundSubjectReceipt, but receipt_id is additionally constrained to the closed candr_ namespace -- mirrors WindowBoundReceipt's own reasoning exactly.

StructureNeedKind.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: the closed enum for which intent-frame member is missing or ambiguous (pivot-intent design brief section 2.1).

StructureOfferSource.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: closed vocabulary distinguishing an engine-derived offer from a Bridge-proposed one (design brief section 2.1/2.4).

KindOption.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: one server-offered census-kind choice, minted onto a stored result so a later turn can confirm it via kindr_ receipt redemption.

AnchorOption.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: one server-offered unique-claimant anchor candidate, minted onto a stored result so a later turn can confirm it via ancr_ receipt redemption. Re-verification identity is (kind, canonical_id, matched_term_hash) -- see internal/contextfabric's verifyAnchorClaimantUnique. matched_term_hash is the SHA-256 digest of the normalized matched term, never the raw term.

CandidateOption.description: CHAOS-4012: one server-offered top-ranked SubjectCandidate from the resolution's own pool, minted onto a stored result so a later turn can confirm it via candr_ receipt redemption. Fires independently of KindOption above -- offered whenever nothing committed and the pool is non-empty, regardless of how many distinct kinds it spans. Field shape mirrors AnchorOption minus matched_term_hash: a candidate claims no per-term uniqueness, so there is no hash to re-verify.

AnchorOptionV2.description: CHAOS-4042 (sol-max ruling): one server-offered anchor candidate under MEMBERSHIP-VERIFY semantics -- the claimant set is NOT required to be unique. Redemption re-verifies that (kind, canonical_id) remains a member of the term's complete claimant set at the pinned ResolvedGraphBinding epoch, matched by (matched_term_hash, kind, canonical_id) together, never id or hash alone. Wire shape is identical to v1 AnchorOption; only the meaning differs, which is why this is a distinct, permanently-separate contract rather than a v1 revision. Only ever carried on a result whose schema_version is context_fabric_investigation_result.v2 -- a v1 result (context_fabric_investigation_result.v1) uses AnchorOption and stays unique-claimant permanently.

HandleOption.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: one server-offered grammar-valid handle candidate, minted onto a stored result so a later turn can confirm it via handr_ receipt redemption. pattern_id names the closed handle-grammar registry pattern -- never regex text on the wire.

AcceptedGrammar.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: discloses one grammar the engine accepts for explicit supply (design brief section 2.1). pattern_id is registry-pinned, never regex text.

StructureNeeds.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: the disclosure block -- present whenever an investigation round ends short of decisive. relation_family and cohort_shape are unrepresentable here by design (design brief section 1.1's demotion).

StructureNeedsV2.description: CHAOS-4042: the disclosure block carried on a context_fabric_investigation_result.v2 result -- identical to StructureNeeds except anchor_options items are AnchorOptionV2 (membership-verify semantics) rather than AnchorOption (unique-claimant). kind_options/handle_options/window_options/accepted_grammars are unchanged from v1.

StructureSource.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: closed vocabulary for how a ConfirmedStructureEntry's value entered (design brief section 2.1's echo).

WindowConfirmationMode.description: CHAOS-3900 W2, design brief section 4/DW3: closed vocabulary for how a caller wants an INFERRED (non-confirmed) evidence window disclosed. Both modes carry the same WindowClarification/EffectiveEvidenceWindow data; the mode only controls whether the disclosure is also nudged through Warnings. The empty string is the caller's own 'not set' state, mapped to headless by the engine. CHAOS-4040 (sol-max ruling 2026-08-21): every inferred window is gated out of decisive terminals regardless of this field, so the mode selects the nudge sentence on that confirmation-required terminal, not between a nudge and an otherwise-decisive answer.

RequestedHandle.description: CHAOS-3972 P3, design brief section 2.3: one caller-supplied explicit subject_handle value -- a typed (kind, pattern_id, value) triple the engine grammar-validates before it may become a receipt-bound HandleOption offer.

StructureProvenance.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: closed authority-tier vocabulary for a ConfirmedStructureEntry (design brief section 2.0's authority table). A distinct enum from WindowProvenance despite sharing the same three values -- each frame member owns its own authority vocabulary independently.

StructureDisposition.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: closed vocabulary for what happened to one carried structure member (design brief section 2.1's silent-drop closure).

ConfirmedStructureEntry.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: the wire-visible disposition for one carried structure member -- one entry per carried member, including vetoed ones.

StructureOfferSnapshotEntry.description: CHAOS-3900 P1: one echoed offer inside a decisive result's structure_offer_snapshot (design brief section 2.1's B5 gap). Ids/ranks/enums only, never display text.

PriorSubjectReceiptDisposition.description: CHAOS-3478/CHAOS-3813: closed vocabulary for what happened to one PriorSubjectReceipts entry -- unlike StructureDisposition, a skip here never vetoes the investigation (a plural, best-effort conversational hint list degrades per-item by design), it is disclosed instead.

PriorSubjectReceiptDispositionEntry.description: CHAOS-3478/CHAOS-3813: the wire-visible disposition for one PriorSubjectReceipts entry the caller sent -- one entry per carried receipt, including skipped ones.

groups.description: CHAOS-4636: absent on every flat cohort. When present, the cohort-level complete/truncated above are the conjunction/disjunction over these groups, so a reader that ignores groups gets a conservative summary of the whole union rather than a boolean describing only the first group.

rows.description: CHAOS-4347, additive: a renderable table for a fact whose evidence is genuinely a set of rows (e.g. a project's per-team metrics rollup) rather than one scalar. Optional; a claim carries `field`/`value` as its primary scalar either way.

table.description: CHAOS-4637 / CHAOS-4627, additive and OPTIONAL: the producer's own declaration of what `rows` IS -- a closed shape, the composite key that identifies a row, and the measures. Selection keys on this declaration instead of inferring an axis and a set of measures from row geometry, which is what three defeated inferences and one withdrawn rule (dated_fact_trend) cost. ABSENT means undeclared, and an undeclared table is never charted.

AnswerCompleteness.description: CHAOS-4413: promotes the answer-rate/terminal-state measurement (formerly harness-only telemetry, CHAOS-4386) into the public contract. terminal_status/terminal_reason answer WHY the answer stopped where it did; claimed_facts_count/rows_count answer HOW MUCH of an answer is here -- the un-clamped totals, independent of any bounded consumer's own projection budget.

terminal_reason.description: Absent (or empty) exactly when terminal_status is complete -- there is nothing to disclose. Present and one of these closed values on every other status; never the engine's or a model's own raw text.

model_identity.description: CHAOS-3782: the provider/model that produced this result's synthesis, e.g. "openai-compatible/gpt-5-nano". Never a bare vendor name. Optional: rows persisted before this field existed (or by any writer with answer reuse disabled) omit it entirely; absence never blocks reading an existing result, and never makes that result reuse-eligible either (reuse also requires question_hash, absent on the same rows for the same reason). maxLength is provider (<=256) + "/" + model (<=256) = 513, not the 256 shared by every other field here -- those are short deployment/prompt version tokens ACR itself controls.

window_class.description: CHAOS-3900 W1: the model's own sanitized, closed-vocabulary evidence-window classification pick. Absent means the model made no pick.

ClaimedFactRow.description: CHAOS-4347: one row of a claimed fact's OPTIONAL renderable table. A row's own fields are plain scalars -- it never nests another table.

RenderKind.description: CHAOS-4415: the CLOSED vocabulary of renderable answer shapes. Every member is defined now so a consumer can switch exhaustively; only "series" has a producer in slice 1.

RenderPresentation.description: CHAOS-4415: the visual encoding of a "series" shape. Kind names the DATA shape, presentation names the drawing -- a bar chart and a line chart carry identical payloads, so bars are not their own kind.

RenderAxisKind.description: CHAOS-4415: whether a point label is a category name or an ISO-8601 date/date-time. A time axis is positioned by elapsed time, never by index.

RenderShapeRule.description: CHAOS-4415: the CLOSED vocabulary of deterministic selection rules. Exactly one rule produced any given shape; a shape with no rule would be the default-charting this contract forbids.

RenderPointSource.description: CHAOS-4415: where in THIS SAME document a plotted number came from. Validation resolves it and requires exact equality, so a chart number can never be authored, re-derived, rounded or aggregated.

RenderPoint.description: CHAOS-4415: one plotted number and its provenance.

RenderSeries.description: CHAOS-4415: one named line/bar family within a shape. A series with no point for a label has a genuine gap there -- never a zero.

RenderShape.description: CHAOS-4415: ONE renderable shape an answer carries, selected by a deterministic rule from the interpreted intent and the facts the answer already holds. Conditional on intent, never default.

CohortGroup.description: CHAOS-4636: one group of a GROUPED cohort answer. Members are named by canonical id into Cohort.members rather than nested, so the flattened member list stays authoritative and a grouped answer does not pay for every member twice against the byte budget. A group carries its OWN complete/truncated, which is the representation the flat cohort booleans could not express.

QuestionFamily.description: CHAOS-4636 (promoted from CHAOS-4632's shadow vocabulary once its false-emission rate was measured on real data). The closed question-family vocabulary. It does not replace InvestigationShape.

QuestionFamilySource.description: How a family was reached. On the wire beside the family because "the model said so at N=1" and "carried from the previous turn" are different warrants for the same value.

PlanNarrowingStage.description: The three moments a plan may narrow. Three, because the budgets become knowable at three different times: cardinality is all that is knowable pre-read; synthesis CREATES the drivers/findings/claims the item budget charges, so pre-synthesis can only bound its INPUTS; and only the assembled result can be measured.

NarrowingBasis.description: The declared order a narrowing step takes members in. canonical_id_lexical is ARBITRARY and says so -- what a pre-read guard needs is stability, not relevance. attention_rank exists only after the fact read.

BudgetOverrun.description: Which budget axis an assembled answer exceeded.

PlanNarrowing.description: One recorded narrowing step. On the wire because it IS the disclosure: "showing 2 of 3 teams, 3 of N projects each" is a useful partial answer only if the caller is told.

AnswerPlanBudget.description: The ceiling the plan was built against and the headroom it reserved, persisted so an over-budget answer names the number that was wrong.

AnswerPlan.description: CHAOS-4636: what the question was PLANNED to be answered with, produced by a deterministic stage between interpretation and discovery. Declares which render kinds the question authorizes (so a chart is never drawn merely because the geometry allowed it), which fact kinds it needs, and the budget it was built against.

ClaimedFactTable.description: CHAOS-4637: the declaration of what a fact's row table is. Carries no rows of its own -- it describes the rows carried beside it, so a declaration can never double a table's bytes against the response budget.

field.description: The canonical fact field the rows came from. A fact may carry more than one row-shaped field, so a declaration that did not name its own field would describe an unidentified table.

shape.description: What the table IS. `time_series` is one entity indexed by an instant (exactly one key column, parsing as an instant on every row); `breakdown` is many entities with one observation each; `ranking` is many entities ordered by the measure `order_by` names.

key.description: The COMPOSITE identity of a row, in declared order. Names ROW columns only -- row identity is relative to the fact's own subject, which is carried by `subject` and is never duplicated here. Exactly one column for `time_series`.

measures.description: The columns that MEASURE something. A measure may legitimately be absent from an individual row; a key column may not.

order_by.description: For `ranking` only: which declared measure the row order is by.
